item.title: Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage Coinbase (COIN) has opened crypto spot margin trading to U.S. customers, letting eligible traders borrow to go long or short with up to 10x leverage, the exchange announced Wednesday, though access is limited to investors with more than $10 million invested. “Crypto spot margin is now available in the US for eligible traders,” Coinbase wrote on X. Traders borrow at the moment they place an order, rather than setting up a loan first. The eligibility bar is high. In a follow-up post , Coinbase said margin trading is open only to people who qualify as “eligible contract participants” under the Commodity Exchange Act. For an individual, that generally means more than $10 million in assets invested on a discretionary basis. The product is also not available in all states, and the loans are for commercial or business purposes only, the company said. Coinbase did not list eligible states or assets in the posts. The limit tracks how U.S. law treats leverage. Under the Commodity Exchange Act , leveraged retail commodity trades generally have to run through a regulated futures exchange, so off-exchange margin products like this one are often reserved for eligible contract participants. How spot margin works Coinbase first described spot margin in October. Eligible traders can borrow against collateral to increase their buying power on spot markets, with leverage of up to 10x on selected major assets and up to 5x on other supported assets. Collateral can be posted in more than 15 supported assets and stays on Coinbase throughout. Loan balances, collateral levels and margin health appear in real time, and spot positions sit in the same margin portfolio as a trader’s derivatives. For U.S. customers, Coinbase Credit, Inc. makes the loans and Coinbase, Inc. holds the collateral as custodian. The company said spot margin is not a product of Coinbase Financial Markets, its regulated U.S. futures broker. The risk disclosures are blunt. Variable-rate interest accrues hourly and can erode a trader’s margin level, and market moves can trigger margin calls or automatic liquidation. In October, the company warned that collateral “may be liquidated without notice” and that traders can lose more than their initial deposit. Part of a bigger trading push from Coinbase Spot margin is one piece of what Coinbase calls its “Everything Exchange.” In the same October post, it said its integration of Deribit was complete and that crypto options, spot margin and unified portfolios would roll out in the coming weeks. That push leans on guidance the Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued in May, which Coinbase said made Coinbase Financial Markets the only U.S. futures commission merchant able to connect U.S. clients to global crypto derivatives liquidity. item.title: Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin Russia’s central bank plans to let ordinary investors trade bitcoin and other crypto on margin, capped at 300,000 rubles with a broker, a senior Bank of Russia official said this week, days after retail buying became legal. Olga Shishlyannikova, director of the central bank’s department of investment financial intermediaries, outlined the plan at the Ural Conference hosted by NAUFOR, the national association of securities market participants, RBC Investments reported. She said the margin rule and two other acts are under review at Russia’s Justice Ministry, and the regulator expects them to be registered by the end of 2026. It is not yet clear whether the 300,000-ruble margin limit for non-qualified investors will be shared with the existing cap on crypto purchases or counted separately. The central bank first published draft margin rules in July. Under that draft, brokers could accept cryptocurrencies as collateral for margin positions, and their clients could sell short. Both qualified and non-qualified investors would be able to trade on margin, with retail crypto trades subject to limits set by the Bank of Russia. The draft also added crypto to the risk-coverage ratios brokers use to police leveraged trades. Those ratios set how far a broker can lend against a client’s portfolio and when positions are forcibly closed. Crypto funds expected in 2027 Shishlyannikova also said the central bank expects the first Russian mutual funds that hold crypto directly to appear in 2027. Professional market participants have already filed applications to register such funds, she said. “Yes, we are considering the possibility next year of amending the relevant regulations to allow funds intended for qualified investors to buy cryptocurrency,” Shishlyannikova said. The regulator is not considering the same access for funds sold to non-qualified investors, she added. In late September, the central bank allowed fund managers to invest qualified investors’ money in cash-settled instruments tied to crypto prices, in a directive registered with the Justice Ministry. The proposed change would let those funds hold the coins themselves. Futures for retail can wait Retail access to crypto futures will take longer. Deputy Governor Philipp Gabunia told reporters on Thursday that the Bank of Russia could let non-qualified investors trade crypto-linked futures once the spot market is running, if it sees no risks, Interfax reported. “For non-qualified investors, this could be a very sensitive story. Let’s launch, and now we’ll see how it starts to work,” Gabunia said. “If we don’t see risks, we’ll allow it. Non-qualified investors will have to be a little patient.” Gabunia said the market’s shape could still shift, including which coins are admitted and which derivatives are offered on them. “Legislation is now changing this configuration a lot,” he said. item.title: Bitcoin Price Rebounds Near $64,000 as Anthropic IPO Lifts Tech Stocks
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Rebounds Near $64,000 as Anthropic IPO Lifts Tech Stocks The bitcoin price climbed back to near $63,700 on Thursday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, as Anthropic’s record initial public offering lifted tech stocks and stock futures ahead of the U.S. open. Bitcoin dipped near $62,000 late Wednesday after Federal Reserve minutes pointed to more rate hikes. It recovered overnight and briefly touched about $64,000 around 6 a.m. ET before easing slightly. The bitcoin price remains down roughly 11% from a week ago, when it traded above $71,000, and more than 20% below the roughly $82,200 level of a month ago. Anthropic IPO lifts risk appetite Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, above its $70 to $78 range. The company sold about 980 million shares and raised $81.3 billion, topping SpaceX’s record offering in June, CNBC reported . The stock is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT, with a fully diluted value of about $1.5 trillion. The pricing sent Nasdaq-100 futures up 2% early Thursday, while S&P 500 futures added 1.1% and Dow futures rose about 299 points. Chipmakers led the move, with Nvidia (NVDA) up 1.5% and Micron Technology (MU) up almost 5% in premarket trading. Some analysts had argued that investors were selling bitcoin to raise cash for the deal. Others questioned how much that selling actually weighed on the bitcoin price. With pricing now done, the bounce in crypto has tracked the broader rebound in tech. Gray market trading pointed to Anthropic shares opening as much as 24% above the IPO price. Crypto stocks rebound before the open Strategy (MSTR) traded near $93.90 before the bell, up about 4% after closing Wednesday at $90.32, down 6.4%. The company’s shares have fallen sharply alongside the bitcoin price this month, and a New York state pension fund boosted its Strategy stake by more than 10% in the third quarter, a 13F filing showed. Coinbase (COIN) rose about 3% in premarket trading to near $114 after a nearly 4% drop on Wednesday. Bitcoin miners also moved higher. Riot Platforms (RIOT) gained about 6%, extending Wednesday’s 7% rally, while MARA Holdings (MARA) and IREN (IREN) each climbed about 4% to 5%. ETF outflows and Fed risk weigh on the bitcoin price Demand from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs remains weak. The funds shed a net $306.5 million on Wednesday, led by $148.7 million out of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) and $69.3 million from Fidelity’s FBTC. The ETFs have posted net outflows on 10 of the last 12 trading days. The Fed is still the main headwind. Minutes from the October meeting showed that almost all officials judged further rate hikes “would likely be appropriate,” and a couple noted that a larger increase might be needed in December. item.title: Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said . Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11. Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together. How the scheme worked From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors said. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information. The group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over. The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims. The BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme. From Scotland to a California courtroom Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC said . Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim. Buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples. Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed , that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since. What Scattered Spider is Reuters has described Scattered Spider as a loose-knit community of hackers suspected of breaking into dozens of U.S. companies. item.title: Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds Binance says it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers. Reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to. “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss said. What is frozen Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report . That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it says was affected. Most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts. The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice says government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva said the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action. How the hack unfolded Binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the company said. From there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance. The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has said the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster. That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. item.title: Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’ K33 Research said bitcoin is trading in “deep value territory” after a 14% weekly drop, arguing that “any entry below $70K is a gift from the market” for medium- to long-term investors. The call comes in the firm’s weekly report, “No gain, plenty of pain,” which published Nov. 16. Head of research Vetle Lunde wrote that bitcoin’s slide has erased its August and September gains and left the market deeply oversold. Bitcoin has posted six straight red weekly candles and is on track for a record 13 consecutive days of lower daily highs, according to K33. Lunde said a streak of six weekly losses has happened only twice before, from Jan. 26 to March 1, 2026, and from April 3 to May 29, 2022. Daily RSI, a momentum gauge, hit 19.95 on Saturday and has stayed below 25 since Friday. Bitcoin also fell below its 200-week moving average, near $68,000, after its worst weekly return since June 7. Bitcoin below its long-term average At the bottom on Nov. 15, bitcoin traded about 8.5% under the 200-week average, a wider gap than the 7.3% recorded at June’s low of $58,500. K33 said 51.5% of the bitcoin supply last moved on-chain at prices above the current level, meaning the average holder could have sold for more at some point in the past four years. Lunde said those readings, taken together, have typically lined up with market bottoms. K33 also noted that crypto has lagged traditional markets, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recovering modestly last week while bitcoin sank. Bitcoin was trading near $62,300 on Wednesday, according to Coinbase spot prices, below the roughly $65,000 level cited in the K33 report, which showed bitcoin down 14% on the week and about 20% over 30 days. Ether also fell 14% over the week, to around $1,827. Outflows, liquidations and hedging Capital continues to leave bitcoin funds. Net outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded products reached 44,900 BTC over the 14 trading days since Oct. 29, K33 said, short of the record of about 71,000 BTC set in June. Total ETF holdings fell to about 1.46 million BTC, the lowest since Aug. 19, and leveraged ETF exposure dropped to 21,900 BTC, the lowest since March 2024. Forced selling hit derivatives, too. About $1.3 billion in long positions were liquidated on Nov. 13 and 14 as bitcoin broke below $70,000, K33 said, and funding rates on perpetual futures repeatedly turned negative. Open interest fell by about 30,000 BTC but stayed above 330,000 BTC, leaving leverage elevated against historical norms. Institutional futures players largely stayed on the sidelines. Open interest in bitcoin futures on CME stayed below 100,000 BTC all week, K33 said, a sign that regulated-market participants have not rushed in to buy the dip. Demand for downside protection is also surging.
